text: Which expression correctly states Bayes' theorem for the posterior credence in a hypothesis H given evidence E?
explanation: Bayes' theorem is P(H|E) = P(E|H) x P(H) / P(E): the posterior equals the likelihood times the prior, divided by the marginal probability of the evidence. Option 0 swaps the prior P(H) with the evidence term P(E); option 1 divides by the likelihood instead of multiplying by it; option 2 drops the likelihood entirely. Only option 3 is the correct rearrangement of the definition of conditional probability.
